track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Cape Gloucester (7th Marine Regiment in 1st Marine Division, 26 December 1943). Wikipedia 7th Marine Regiment. Confirm against 7th Marines AAR.

track.note: 15 September 1944, Peleliu. 7th Marines landed Orange Beach 3; 1st Marines White, 5th Marines Orange centre. Grain vs 1st Marines already on this commune. Okinawa (Dakeshi / Wana) is not pinned until a distinct named commune is sourced.
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Peleliu (7th Marines landed Orange Beach 3, 15 September 1944). Wikipedia 7th Marine Regiment. Published location, Peleliu. Confirm against 7th Marines AAR.

name: 27th Marine Regiment
source: 27th Marines first saw action on Iwo Jima with 5th Marine Division, which landed Red 1, Red 2, and Green 1 on 19 February 1945. 26th Marines was the afternoon reserve; 28th Marines is the Suribachi 23 February pin. Confirm against 27th Marines AAR.

track.note: 19 February 1945, Iwo Jima. 27th Marines with 5th Marine Division on the Red/Green landing beaches at the base of Suribachi. Grain vs 28th Marines (Suribachi 23 February) and the 4th/5th Marine Division landing pins. 26th Marines was released as division reserve that afternoon.
track.source: Wikipedia 27th Marine Regiment (first action Iwo Jima); Wikipedia 5th Marine Division (landed Red 1, Red 2, Green 1 on 19 February 1945). Confirm against 27th Marines AAR.

name: USS Oklahoma
source: USS Oklahoma (BB-37) capsized on Battleship Row, Pearl Harbor, 7 December 1941. Harbour pin matches Arizona; do not use the 1947 tow-sinking position. Confirm against US Navy after-action reports.

track.note: 7 December 1941, Pearl Harbor. Capsized on Battleship Row. Coarser pin on the harbour, same as Arizona. Infobox 24°58′N 150°6′W is the 1947 hulk sinking under tow, not this pin.
track.source: Wikipedia USS Oklahoma (BB-37); published location, Pearl Harbor. Confirm against US Navy after-action reports.

name: USS West Virginia
source: USS West Virginia (BB-48) was moored on Battleship Row on 7 December 1941, sank in shallow water, and was later rebuilt. Harbour pin matches Arizona. Confirm against US Navy after-action reports.

track.note: 7 December 1941, Pearl Harbor. Moored on Battleship Row; torpedoed and sank in shallow water. Coarser pin on the harbour, same as Arizona. Surigao Strait / Iwo / Okinawa on this ship are not pinned this pass.
track.source: Wikipedia USS West Virginia (BB-48); published location, Pearl Harbor. Confirm against US Navy after-action reports.

name: 31st Division (IJA)
source: IJA 31st Division (Furious / Retsu Heidan) at Kohima. Distinct from Hub jp-31st-army (Marianas garrison). Confirm against 31st Division records.

track.note: 5 April 1944, Kohima. Miyazaki's probe 3 April; siege preparations 6 April. Opposite 7th Indian Division on the same commune. Do not alias to Hub jp-31st-army (Saipan/Guam/Tinian).
track.source: Wikipedia 31st Division (Imperial Japanese Army), Battle of Kohima. Published commune location, Kohima. Confirm against 31st Division records.

name: 90th Light Afrika Division
source: 90th Light Infantry Division (90th Light Afrika) fought at First and Second El Alamein and surrendered in Tunisia. Grain vs 21st Panzer and Ariete on the same commune. Confirm against division KTB.

track.note: 1 July 1942, El Alamein. 90th Light attacked along the coast toward the Alamein position at First Alamein. Hub first-el-alamein. Second Alamein remains 23 October.
track.source: Hub 90th Light Africa Division (first-el-alamein). Wikipedia 90th Light Infantry Division (First El Alamein). Published commune location, El Alamein. Confirm against 90th Light KTB.

track.note: 23 October 1942, El Alamein. 90th Light with Panzer Army Africa at Second Alamein. Grain vs 21st Panzer, Ariete, and 2nd New Zealand Division on the same commune.
track.source: Wikipedia 90th Light Infantry Division (First and Second El Alamein). Published commune location, El Alamein. Confirm against 90th Light KTB.

track.note: 13 May 1943, Tunis. Surrender in Tunisia. Do not continue this id as 90th Panzergrenadier in Italy.
track.source: Hub 90th Light Africa Division (tunisia). Published commune location, Tunis (reuse pack 10.1817, 36.8064). Confirm against 90th Light KTB.

name: Hermann Göring Division
source: Panzer-Division Hermann Göring counter-attacked the Gela beachhead 11 July 1943 and fought the Battle of Cisterna 30 January 1944 opposite US Rangers and 3rd Infantry. Confirm against division KTB.

track.note: 11 July 1943, Gela beachhead. HG with Livorno Division in the amphibious counter-attack, forced back by naval gunfire. Grain vs US 1st Infantry on Gela 10 July.
track.source: Wikipedia 1st Fallschirm-Panzer Division Hermann Göring (Battle of Gela 10–11 July 1943). Published commune location, Gela. Confirm against HG KTB.

track.note: 30 January 1944, Cisterna di Latina. HG on the German left flank of the Battle of Cisterna, facing US 3rd Infantry and 1st/3rd Rangers. Opposite us-1-rangers on the same commune.
track.source: Wikipedia 1st Fallschirm-Panzer Division Hermann Göring (Battle of Cisterna). Published commune location, Cisterna di Latina. Confirm against HG KTB.

name: 22nd Battalion (New Zealand)
source: 22nd Battalion (Andrew) was the main New Zealand unit at Maleme airfield, 20 May 1941. Do not smear 2nd New Zealand Division onto the airfield. Confirm against the battalion war diary.

track.note: 20 May 1941, Maleme. 22nd Battalion held Hill 107 covering the airfield; Andrew withdrew that night. Opposite 7th Flieger Division. Explicit italy tag: Maleme sits south of the Italy bound. 2nd New Zealand Division stays on El Alamein / Cassino.
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Maleme (main New Zealand unit at Maleme was 22nd Battalion). Wikipedia Maleme. Confirm against 22nd Battalion war diary.

name: No. 3 Commando
source: World extra date for Operation Devon. Normandy file keeps Amfreville 6 June. Map-only (Hub uk-commandos maps to 47 RM).

track.note: 3 October 1943, Termoli. Operation Devon seaborne landing with No. 40 RM Commando and the Special Raiding Squadron; 78th Division brigades arrived as relief. Distinct from 78th Division on the same commune. Normandy file keeps Amfreville.
track.source: Wikipedia Operation Devon (No. 3 Commando, 3–6 October 1943). Wikipedia Termoli. Confirm against the commando war diary.

name: 1re Brigade Française Libre
source: 1re Brigade Française Libre (Koenig) held Bir Hakeim, 26 May – 11 June 1942. Do not extra onto Hub fr-1e-dfl (tunisia / Cassino / italy-end only). Confirm against Free French records.

track.note: 26 May 1942, Bir Hakeim. 1re BFL (Koenig) opened the Gazala southern-box defence against Ariete, then Trieste and 90th Light. Map-only: Hub 1re DFL stays Tunis / Cassino.
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Bir Hakeim (Free French under Koenig, 26 May – 11 June 1942). Wikipedia Bir Hakeim. Confirm against Free French records.

name: 1st Marine Raider Battalion
source: Edson's 1st Raider Battalion landed Tulagi 7 August 1942. Do not smear onto Hub us-2nd-marines (2nd Marine Division at Betio / Saipan). Confirm against 1st Raider Battalion records.

track.note: 7 August 1942, Tulagi. 1st Marine Raider Battalion (Edson) landed as the opening of Watchtower. Distinct from 1st Marines at Honiara and from 2nd Marine Division (Betio / Saipan). 2nd Marines 1/2 on Florida Island that morning is not pinned on the division id.
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Tulagi and Gavutu–Tanambogo; Wikipedia Marine Raiders (Edson's 1st Raider Battalion landed Tulagi 7 August 1942). Wikipedia Tulagi. Confirm against 1st Raider Battalion records.

name: 1st Marine Defense Battalion
source: 1st Marine Defense Battalion (Devereux) garrisoned Wake Island when the Japanese attack opened 8 December 1941 (7 December Hawaii time). Confirm against 1st Defense Battalion records.

track.note: 8 December 1941, Wake Island. 1st Marine Defense Battalion opened the defence the same calendar day as Pearl (west of the date line). Surrender is 23 December, not a second pin.
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Wake Island (1st Marine Defense Battalion, 8–23 December 1941). Wikipedia Wake Island. Confirm against 1st Defense Battalion records.

name: 4th Infantry Division Livorno
source: Livorno Division counter-attacked the Gela beachhead 11 July 1943. Opposite 1st Infantry Division. Confirm against Italian Army Historical Branch.

track.note: 11 July 1943, Gela. Livorno Division three-prong infantry/tank counter-attack on the Husky beachhead, same day as Hermann Göring. Opposite US 1st Infantry Division (Gela 10 July landing pin).
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Gela (1943) (Livorno Division counter-attack 11 July). Published commune location, Gela. Confirm against Italian Army Historical Branch.

name: 4th Fallschirmjäger Division
source: 4. Fallschirmjäger-Division first combat was against the Anzio landings, January 1944. Distinct from 1st FJ at Cassino. Confirm against I Fallschirmkorps records.

track.note: 22 January 1944, Anzio. 4th Fallschirmjäger Division (Trettner), I Fallschirmkorps, first combat against Operation Shingle. Distinct from 1st FJ at Cassino and from HG at Cisterna 30 January. Coarser division pin on the beachhead commune.
track.source: Wikipedia 4th Parachute Division (first combat Anzio, January 1944). Published location, Anzio. Confirm against I Fallschirmkorps records.

name: 18th Australian Brigade
source: 18th Brigade (7th Australian Division) at Giarabub, Milne Bay, Sanananda, and Balikpapan. Map-only grain vs Hub au-7th-div (Kokoda-only card). Confirm against AWM 18th Brigade records.

track.note: 21 March 1941, Jaghbub (Giarabub). 2/9th Battalion led the assault on the Italian fortress; the garrison surrendered the same afternoon. First combat pin of the brigade.
track.source: Wikipedia 18th Brigade (Australia) (Giarabub assault 21 March 1941). Wikipedia Jaghbub. Confirm against AWM 18th Brigade records.

track.note: 27 August 1942, Alotau / Milne Bay. 18th Brigade (Wootten) in the land battle through 7 September, the first major Japanese land defeat of the war. Grain vs Japanese 18th Army on the same published town. Do not extra onto Hub au-7th-div (Kokoda-only card).
track.source: Wikipedia 18th Brigade (Australia) (Milne Bay 27 August–7 September 1942). Wikipedia Battle of Milne Bay. Published named-place location, Alotau (same pin as jp-18th-army). Confirm against AWM 18th Brigade records.

track.note: 21 January 1943, Sanananda. 18th Brigade captured the Papuan beachhead with US 163rd Infantry. Distinct from Milne Bay.
track.source: Wikipedia 18th Brigade (Australia) (captured Sanananda 21 January 1943). Wikipedia Sanananda. Confirm against AWM 18th Brigade records.

track.note: 1 July 1945, Balikpapan. 18th Brigade in the first wave around Klandasan; took the town 3 July. Last sourced pin of the brigade.
track.source: Wikipedia 18th Brigade (Australia) (landed Balikpapan 1 July 1945). Wikipedia Balikpapan. Confirm against AWM 18th Brigade records.

name: 172nd Infantry Regiment
source: 172nd Infantry (43rd Infantry Division) in the capture of Munda airfield, 5 August 1943. Map-only: Hub us-43rd-inf is Guadalcanal-only. Confirm against 43rd Infantry Division records.

track.note: 5 August 1943, Munda. 172nd Infantry, 43rd Infantry Division (Winged Victory), in the capture of Munda Point airfield ending the Battle of Munda Point. Map-only regiment grain: do not extra Munda onto Hub us-43rd-inf (Guadalcanal-only card).
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Munda Point (airfield captured 5 August 1943; 43rd Infantry Division from 2 July). Wikipedia Munda, Solomon Islands. CMH 43d Infantry Division combat chronicle. Confirm against 172nd Infantry Regiment records.

name: 148th Infantry Regiment
source: 148th Infantry (37th Infantry Division) landed at Cape Torokina 8 November 1943. Map-only: Hub us-37th-inf and us-3rd-marines do not list Bougainville. Confirm against 37th Infantry Division records.

track.note: 8 November 1943, Cape Torokina. 148th Infantry, 37th Infantry Division (Buckeye), first Army regiment ashore at Empress Augusta Bay, following 3rd Marine Division's 1 November landing. Map-only: do not extra Torokina onto Hub us-3rd-marines (Guadalcanal + Iwo) or us-37th-inf (Guadalcanal-only card).
track.source: Wikipedia Landings at Cape Torokina (6.235 S, 155.035 E). US Army photo caption 37th Division troops for Bougainville beach 8 November 1943. armydivs.com 37th Infantry Division (148th Infantry landed 8 November). Confirm against 148th Infantry Regiment records.

name: British 52nd (Lowland) Infantry Division
source: 52nd (Lowland) at Cherbourg 15 June 1940 (Operation Aerial) and Ringenberg 26 March 1945 (Rhine breakout). Hub lists dunkirk + rhine. Confirm against TNA WO 167 / WO 171 52nd Division records.

track.note: 15 June 1940, Cherbourg. 52nd (Lowland) of the Second BEF embarked 15–17 June during Operation Aerial, covering the withdrawal after Dunkirk. Not the Dunkirk town pin. Explicit nw-europe: Cherbourg also sits in the Normandy frame.
track.source: Wikipedia 52nd (Lowland) Infantry Division (2BEF, Operation Aerial near Cherbourg). Wikipedia Operation Aerial (most of 52nd embarked Cherbourg 15–17 June 1940). Published commune location, Cherbourg-en-Cotentin. Confirm against TNA WO 167 52nd Division records.

track.note: 26 March 1945, Ringenberg. 52nd (Lowland) advanced from the Bislich Rhine bridgehead and captured the village by evening. Distinct from 15th Scottish Division's 24 March Bislich assault crossing. Not Dunkirk town.
track.source: krieg-am-niederrhein.de The Assault Across the Rhine (52nd Scottish Infantry Division from Bislich captured Ringenberg by the evening of 26 March 1945). German Wikipedia Ringenberg (51.741699 N, 6.610831 E). Confirm against TNA WO 171 52nd Division records.

name: 14th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS
source: 14. Waffen-Grenadier-Division der SS (galizische Nr. 1) in the Brody pocket, July 1944. Hub battleId bagration (card names Brody). Confirm against Bundesarchiv Militärarchiv.

track.note: 13 July 1944, Brody. 14th SS (Galicia) holding the XIII Corps sector when 1st Ukrainian Front opened the Lviv–Sandomierz offensive; the Brody pocket closed 18 July. Distinct from 1st Ukrainian Front at Lviv. Coarser division pin on the town.
track.source: Wikipedia 14th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS (1st Galician) (Brody, July 1944). Wikipedia Brody. Ukrainian Wikipedia Battle of Brody 13–22 July 1944. Confirm against Bundesarchiv Militärarchiv.

name: Polish Army Prusy
source: Army Prusy northern group fought at Tomaszów Mazowiecki 5–6 September 1939. Hub battleId invasion-of-poland. Confirm against Polish Army Prusy records.

track.note: 5 September 1939, Tomaszów Mazowiecki. Army Prusy northern group (13th, 19th, 29th Infantry and Wilno Cavalry) in the Piotrków–Tomaszów battles 5–6 September against German XVI Panzer Corps. Still assembling on 1 September; this is the combat pin.
track.source: Wikipedia Prussian Army (Polish Armed Forces) (battles of Piotrków and Tomaszów Mazowiecki 5–6 September). Wikipedia Tomaszów Mazowiecki (51.517 N, 20.017 E). Confirm against Polish Army Prusy records.

name: Polish Army Karpaty
source: Karpaty Army attacked at Czorsztyn on 1 September 1939. Hub battleId invasion-of-poland. Confirm against Polish Army Karpaty records.

track.note: 1 September 1939, Czorsztyn. Karpaty Army attacked in the morning by German 4th Light Division supported by 2nd Mountain Division on the Carpathian frontier. Coarser army pin on the named village.
track.source: Wikipedia Carpathian Army (attacked in the area of Czorsztyn on 1 September by 4th Light Division). Wikipedia Czorsztyn (49.433 N, 20.317 E). Confirm against Polish Army Karpaty records.

name: Independent Operational Group Narew
source: SGO Narew manned the Narew line at Łomża on 1 September 1939. Hub battleId invasion-of-poland. Confirm against SGO Narew records.

track.note: 1 September 1939, Łomża. Independent Operational Group Narew manned the Narew river line from dawn, with HQ in Łomża ready to move to Śniadowo. Coarser army pin on the named town. Wizna 7–10 September is a later fight.
track.source: Wikipedia Battle of Łomża (1939) (Narew line manned by SGO Narew; Łomża on the southern bank). Polish Wikipedia SGO Narew (HQ in Łomża 31 August, positions occupied at dawn 1 September). Wikipedia Łomża (53.17639 N, 22.07306 E). Confirm against SGO Narew records.

name: US 5th Infantry Division
source: CMH 5th Infantry Division combat chronicle: Caumont 13 July 1944, Angers 9–10 August, Echternach 26 December, Oppenheim Rhine crossing 22 March 1945. Hub battleIds normandy, bulge, rhine. Confirm against 5th Infantry Division records.

track.note: 13 July 1944, Caumont-l'Éventé. 5th Infantry Division landed Utah Beach 9 July (beach, not a commune) and four days later took up defensive positions in the vicinity of Caumont. Coarser division pin on the named commune.
track.source: CMH 5th Infantry Division combat chronicle (landed Utah Beach 9 July 1944; four days later defensive positions in the vicinity of Caumont). Wikipedia Caumont-l'Éventé (49.0911 N, 0.8039 W). Confirm against 5th Infantry Division records.

track.note: 9 August 1944, Angers. Division captured the city 9–10 August after the Cobra breakout. South of the Normandy camera frame; tagged nw-europe.
track.source: CMH 5th Infantry Division combat chronicle (attacked and captured Angers, 9–10 August 1944). Wikipedia Angers (47.47111 N, 0.55194 W). Confirm against 5th Infantry Division records.

track.note: 26 December 1944, Echternach. 10th Infantry of 5th Infantry Division walked into the town in the early hours after XII Corps' southern-shoulder attack from 22 December. Distinct from 4th Infantry, which held Echternach on 16 December.
track.source: Army Historical Foundation, The Battle for Echternach (10th Infantry walked into Echternach in the early hours of 26 December 1944). CMH 5th Infantry Division combat chronicle (thrown in against the southern flank of the Bulge 18 December). Wikipedia Echternach (49.8116667 N, 6.4216667 E). Confirm against 5th Infantry Division records.

track.note: 22 March 1945, Oppenheim. 5th Infantry Division made the Third Army assault crossing of the Rhine at 2200, first US assault crossing of the river. Inside the Hub rhine window (7–24 March).
track.source: CMH 5th Infantry Division combat chronicle (reached and crossed the Rhine, 22 March 1945). US Army CSI Rhine River crossing study (11th Infantry at Oppenheim 2200 22 March). Wikipedia Oppenheim (49.85556 N, 8.36028 E). Confirm against 5th Infantry Division records.

name: US 29th Infantry Division
source: World extra date for Saint-Lô. Normandy file keeps Omaha / Vierville-sur-Mer 6 June.

track.note: 18 July 1944, Saint-Lô. Task Force Cota entered the town about 1800 after 43 days from Omaha. Distinct from 3rd Armored Cobra pin 25 July. Normandy file keeps Vierville-sur-Mer 6 June.
track.source: CMH American Forces in Action, St-Lô (Task Force C of the 29th Division secured the city 18 July). Saint-Lô city liberation itinerary (29th Division entered 18 July). Published commune location, Saint-Lô (reuse pack −1.09, 49.12).

name: 2e Division Blindée
source: World extra date for Alençon. Normandy file keeps Paris 24–25 August.

track.note: 12 August 1944, Alençon. 2e DB took the town overnight 11–12 August. Not Argentan (the division was stopped short of that town). Normandy file keeps Paris 24–25 August.
track.source: Wikipedia 2nd Armored Division (France) (Argentan–Falaise 12–21 August). Voie de la 2e DB / local Alençon liberation (night 11–12 August). Wikipedia Alençon (48.4306 N, 0.0931 E). Confirm against SHD JMO 2e DB.

name: 1st Battalion, Worcestershire Regiment
source: TNA WO 171/1396, 1st Bn Worcestershire Regiment war diary, 22 June 1944. Map-only; do not smear onto British 3rd Division at Sword / Hermanville. 43rd (Wessex) parent.

track.note: 22 June 1944, Crépon. Marching party disembarked LCA at Mont Fleury 1715 and marched to the assembly area at Crépon. Mont Fleury is a hamlet of Ver-sur-Mer (Green Howards stay there). Night move to La Rosière is a lieu-dit, not a second pin. Not British 3rd Division at Hermanville.
track.source: WO 171/1396 (worcestershireregiment.com transcription: Mont Fleury 1715 then assembly Crépon). Hub diary wo171-worcestershire-june. Wikipedia Crépon (49.3169 N, 0.5492 W).

name: 302nd Infantry Division
source: Bundesarchiv RH 26-302 KTB Anlagen Unternehmen Dieppe, 19 August 1942. Map-only German opposite of 2nd Canadian at Dieppe town.

track.note: 19 August 1942, Dieppe. 302nd Infantry Division was the coastal garrison; KTB Ia Nr. 3 is the Gefechtsbericht on the landing at and on both sides of Dieppe. Distinct from 2nd Canadian Division (assault force) and No. 4 Commando at Varengeville. Tagged nw-europe (1942, not the Normandy camera).
track.source: Bundesarchiv RH 26-302/16 Anlagen zum KTB Ia Nr. 3 (Unternehmen Dieppe), 19 Aug 1942. AHQ Report No. 10 (Stacey, German war diaries). Published commune location, Dieppe (reuse pack 1.077, 49.922).

name: 164th Light Africa Division
source: Hub 164th Light Africa Division (second-el-alamein, tunisia). Previously 164th Infantry / Fortress Division Kreta. Confirm against division KTB.

track.note: 23 October 1942, El Alamein. 164th Light Africa with Panzer Army Africa at Second Alamein. Grain vs 90th Light and 21st Panzer on the same commune. Not Fortress Division Kreta.
track.source: Hub 164th Light Africa Division (second-el-alamein). Wikipedia 164th Light Afrika Division. Published commune location, El Alamein. Confirm against 164th Light KTB.

track.note: 13 May 1943, Tunis. Surrender in Tunisia. Do not continue this id as 164th Infantry in Italy.
track.source: Hub 164th Light Africa Division (tunisia). Wikipedia 164th Light Afrika Division. Published commune location, Tunis (reuse pack 10.1817, 36.8064).
